<!-- All news items below this line -->
;Armed conflicts and attacks
*[[2019 Turkish offensive into north-eastern Syria]], [[NES–Syria relations]]
**The [[Syrian Democratic Forces]] agree to allow the [[Syrian Army]] to enter the SDF-held cities of [[Manbij]] and [[Kobani]] in an attempt to deter [[Turkey]] from attacking the towns. [https://thedefensepost.com/2019/10/13/syria-government-russia-kobani-manbij-sdf/ (Defence Post)] [https://www.reuters.com/article/us-syria-security-towns-report/report-syrian-army-to-enter-sdf-held-kobani-manbij-idUSKBN1WS0K0?feedType=RSS&feedName=worldNews&&rpc=401 (Reuters)] [https://english.alarabiya.net/en/News/middle-east/2019/10/13/Syrian-army-to-enter-SDF-held-Kobani-Manbij-Monitor.html (Al Arabiya)]
**As many as 700 [[Islamic State of Iraq and the Levant|ISIL]] family members escape an [[Ayn Issa]] camp. [https://www.cnn.com/2019/10/13/middleeast/turkish-forces-cut-main-road-syria-intl/index.html (CNN)]
**A thousand [[United States Armed Forces|U.S. soldiers]] are to be pulled out of [[Syria]] because of the [[2019 Turkish offensive into north-eastern Syria|Turkish offensive]]. [https://www.bbc.com/news/world-middle-east-50034802 (BBC News)]
**Fourteen people are killed and ten are injured by [[Turkey|Turkish]] airstrikes targeting a convoy in the Syrian town of Ras al Ain. Five are identified as civilians. [https://www.reuters.com/article/us-syria-security-turkey-strike/fourteen-killed-after-turkish-strike-in-ras-al-ain-idUSKBN1WS0HL?il=0 (Reuters)]
*[[Somali Civil War (2009–present)]]
**Multiple mortars hit [[Mogadishu Airport]], wounding at least six people. [[Al-Shabaab (militant group)|Al-Shabaab]] claims responsibility for the attack. [https://www.voanews.com/africa/al-shabab-mortar-attacks-hits-area-around-mogadishu-airport (VOA News)] [https://www.reuters.com/article/us-somalia-security/mortar-bombs-strike-somalias-mogadishu-airport-six-injured-source-idUSKBN1WS0ED (Reuters)]
*[[Russian–Syrian hospital bombing campaign]], [[Russian military intervention in the Syrian Civil War]]
**''[[The New York Times]]'' claims it can prove [[Russia|Russian]] aircraft bombed four [[Syria]]n hospitals in a matter of hours in May, using a combination of logbooks from [[Aircraft spotting|planespotters]], recorded radio transmissions, and eyewitnesses. [https://www.independent.co.uk/news/world/middle-east/russia-syria-bomb-hospitals-war-kurds-putin-assad-idlib-a9153786.html (''The Independent'')]

;Disasters and accidents
*Forty-eight people are confirmed dead, about 100 others are injured and 17 are missing after [[Typhoon Hagibis (2019)|Typhoon Hagibis]] makes landfall in [[Japan]]. [https://news.sky.com/story/typhoon-hagibis-elderly-woman-falls-to-her-death-from-rescue-helicopter-11834366 (Sky News)]
*The 90-metre cargo ship [[ship prefix|MV]] ''Rhodanus'', with a crew of seven, runs aground in the [[Bonifacio, Corse-du-Sud|Mouths of Bonifacio]] nature reserve in the [[Strait of Bonifacio]] off [[Corsica]]. French maritime police say the vessel did not respond to calls for around an hour before grounding, and that fuel was not thought to be leaking. [https://www.france24.com/en/20191013-cargo-ship-runs-aground-in-corsican-nature-reserve (France 24)]
*A gas explosion kills nine people in a restaurant in [[Wuxi]], [[China]]. [https://www.independent.co.uk/news/world/asia/gas-explosion-restaurant-china-death-toll-dead-wuxi-jiangsu-a9154121.html (''The Independent'')]

;International relations
*At [[Saint Peter's Square]], [[Vatican City]], [[Pope Francis]] [[canonization|canonizes]] the 19th-century Anglican convert [[John Henry Newman]], who was a unifying figure in both the [[Anglican Communion|Anglican]] and [[Catholic Church|Catholic church]]es. [http://abcnews.go.com/International/wireStory/pope-canonizes-john-henry-newman-unifier-divided-world-66241676 (ABC News)] 

;Law and crime
*[[California]] becomes the first [[United States|U.S.]] state to ban the sale of [[fur]] products. The law goes into effect on January 1, 2023. [https://edition.cnn.com/2019/10/13/us/california-bans-fur-products-trnd/index.html (CNN)]

;Politics and elections
*[[2019 Tunisian presidential election]]
**Voters in [[Tunisia]] go to the polls to elect a new [[President of Tunisia|president]]. Conservative academic [[Kais Saied]] wins more than 70% of the votes. [https://www.aljazeera.com/news/2019/10/karoui-saied-face-tunisia-presidential-election-191012203427620.html (Al Jazeera)] [https://www.theguardian.com/world/2019/oct/14/tunisia-election-exit-polls-point-to-landslide-win-for-robocop-kais-saied (''The Guardian'')]
*[[2019 Polish parliamentary election]]
**Voters in Poland go to the polls to elect a new government. The incumbent right-wing [[Law and Justice (Poland)|Law and Justice]] is expected to slightly increase its plurality. [https://www.reuters.com/article/us-poland-election/second-term-awaits-nationalist-pis-as-divided-poles-vote-idUSKBN1WR0O4 (Reuters)]
